categoryMeta.description: Flexible speed-play, mixed-effort, time-based, and non-track workouts.

workouts.title: Beginner Introduction to Fartlek
workouts.summary: An easy-going introduction to speed-play using short, light pickups to build basic leg speed safely.
workouts.riskReason: Short running bursts with generous walking recoveries keep impact forces low.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Jog segments very slowly. Speed pick-ups should feel fast but controlled, around 5K effort.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Let heart rate rise naturally during pick-ups, but prioritize breath comfort.

warmup.name: Active Mobilization Walk
warmup.description: 5 mins of slow, purposeful walking with joint circles.

mainSet.name: 5 × 30-Sec Pickups
mainSet.description: Run 30 seconds at a moderately fast but relaxed effort, followed by 90 seconds of walking recovery.

cooldown.name: Walking Cooldown
cooldown.description: 5 mins slow walking to lower heart rate.

easier.description: Reduce main set to 4 repetitions with 2-minute walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: 4 × 30-Sec Pickups
mainSet.description: Run 30 seconds moderately fast, then walk 120 seconds.

harder.description: Increase main set to 6 repetitions with 60-second jogging recoveries.

mainSet.name: 6 × 30-Sec Pickups
mainSet.description: Run 30 seconds moderately fast, then jog easy for 60 seconds.

coachingNotes: Focus on smooth, relaxed running form during the pickups. Do not sprint.
Think of these as 'pickups' rather than hard intervals. Keep them playful.
Enjoy the variation in effort. It shouldn't feel stressful.
safetyNotes: Ensure you are fully warm before attempting the first pickup.
Stop immediately if you feel a sharp pull in your calf or hamstring.

shareCard.purposeText: An easy-going introduction to speed-play to build basic speed safely.

workouts.sourceNote: General running training principles; not personalized medical or coaching advice.

workouts.title: Recreational Landmark Speed Play
workouts.summary: A classic backyard speed play session where you pick visible landmarks to accelerate towards.
workouts.riskReason: Low impact speed play with generous walking recoveries on stable, flat ground.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Easy conversational jog between landmarks. Progress up to moderate-fast running for segments.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Keep overall heart rate modest, with transient peaks during speed play.
intensityGuide.rpeGuide: Base jog RPE 3/10. landmark bursts RPE 5-6/10.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization Walk
warmup.description: 5 mins light joint dynamics and slow walking.

mainSet.name: 6 × Landmark Pickups
mainSet.description: Accelerate continuously for 45 seconds towards a designated landmark (e.g. tree, lamppost), followed by 75 seconds walking/jogging recovery.

cooldown.name: Easy Walking Cooldown
cooldown.description: 5 mins slow walking to ease back to baseline.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 landmark repetitions with 90-second recoveries.

mainSet.name: 4 × Landmark Pickups
mainSet.description: Accelerate 45 seconds towards landmarks, then walk 90 seconds.

harder.description: Increase to 8 landmark repetitions with 60-second jogging recoveries.

mainSet.name: 8 × Landmark Pickups
mainSet.description: Accelerate 45 seconds, then jog 60 seconds.

coachingNotes: Pick landmarks that require about 30 to 50 seconds of running.
Change targets each repetition to keep your focus fresh.
Focus on maintaining high cadence without straining.
commonMistakes: Choosing landmarks that are too far away, forcing a sustained sprint.
Straining at the shoulders and neck trying to run fast.
safetyNotes: Only choose landmarks on flat, safe surfaces without traffic.
Maintain visual awareness of your path to avoid tripping.

shareCard.purposeText: A classic backyard speed play session targeting visual landmarks.

workouts.sourceNote: General running training principles; not personalized medical or coaching advice.

workouts.title: Developing Conversational Fartlek Ladder
workouts.summary: A friendly 1-2-1 minute fartlek ladder designed to introduce structured speed change.
workouts.riskReason: Short progressive efforts with full walking recoveries to keep fatigue low.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Moderate-fast pace for the 1-min efforts, steady conversational pace for the 2-min effort.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Monitor heart rate to ensure it fully drops during walking recoveries.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization Walk
warmup.description: 5 mins slow walking with arm swings.

mainSet.name: 1-2-1 Ladder Pickups
mainSet.description: Run 1 min moderate-fast, walk 90s, run 2 mins steady conversational, walk 90s, run 1 min moderate-fast, walk 90s.

cooldown.name: Gentle Walking Cooldown
cooldown.description: 5 mins slow walking to settle breathing.

easier.description: Reduce to 1 set of the 1-2-1 ladder with 2-minute walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: 1 Set 1-2-1 Ladder
mainSet.description: Run 1 min, walk 120s, run 2 mins, walk 120s, run 1 min, walk 120s.

harder.description: Increase to 3 sets of the 1-2-1 ladder with 60-second jogging recoveries.

mainSet.name: 3 Sets 1-2-1 Ladder
mainSet.description: Run 1 min, jog 60s, run 2 mins, jog 60s, run 1 min, jog 60s.

coachingNotes: The 2-minute pickup should feel distinctly slower and more relaxed than the 1-minute pickups.
Focus on a smooth transition between efforts rather than abrupt jerks.
Keep your breathing rhythmic and controlled.
commonMistakes: Running the 2-minute segment at the same high speed as the 1-minute segments.
Starting the first 1-minute segment too fast.
safetyNotes: Warm up thoroughly before beginning.
Ensure your posture remains tall and vertical during faster phases.

shareCard.mainSetText: 2 Sets of 1-2-1 min Ladder | 90s Walk Recovery
shareCard.purposeText: A friendly 1-2-1 minute ladder to introduce structured speed change.

workouts.title: Intermediate Mona Fartlek Simulation
workouts.summary: A 20-minute classic fartlek simulation with continuous, alternating high and low efforts to build aerobic power.
workouts.riskReason: Continuous speed play segments introduce substantial fatigue and cardiac load.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Pickups are run at 5K effort; recoveries are float efforts, not walking.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate will remain elevated throughout; float recoveries should help prevent redlining.

warmup.name: Joint Mobilization Warm-up
warmup.description: 5 mins light walking with active mobilization drills.

mainSet.name: Mona Block: 2 × 90-Sec
mainSet.description: Run 90 seconds at 5K effort, followed by a 90-second steady float recovery jog.

mainSet.name: Mona Block: 4 × 60-Sec
mainSet.description: Run 60 seconds at 5K effort, followed by a 60-second steady float recovery jog.

mainSet.name: Mona Block: 4 × 30-Sec
mainSet.description: Run 30 seconds at 5K effort, followed by a 30-second steady float recovery jog.

mainSet.name: Mona Block: 4 × 15-Sec
mainSet.description: Run 15 seconds fast, followed by a 15-second steady float recovery jog.

cooldown.name: Light Cooldown Walk
cooldown.description: 5 mins slow walking to ease back to baseline.

easier.description: Reduce reps: 1 × 90s, 2 × 60s, 2 × 30s, 2 × 15s with walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: Reduced Mona Block
mainSet.description: 1 × 90s, 2 × 60s, 2 × 30s, 2 × 15s with equal walking recoveries.

harder.description: Extend block to a full 30 minutes by running two rounds of the 4 × 30s and 4 × 15s segments.

mainSet.name: Extended Mona Block
mainSet.description: Full Mona sequence plus an extra block of 4 × 30s and 4 × 15s.

coachingNotes: The signature of the Mona Fartlek is the float recovery. Do not jog extremely slowly or walk.
Pace the early 90-second segments carefully. The workout gets cumulative very quickly.
Focus on quick foot transitions as the segments get shorter.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the early 90-second segments, making float recoveries impossible.
safetyNotes: Ensure your surface is dry and free of leaves or loose gravel.
Hydrate properly before beginning this high-turnover session.

shareCard.purposeText: A 20-minute classic fartlek with continuous, alternating high/low efforts.

workouts.sourceNote: General running training principles; not personalized medical or coaching advice.

workouts.title: Developing Continuous Aerobic Fartlek
workouts.summary: A 30-minute steady run incorporating periodic threshold pickups to stimulate cardiorespiratory limits safely.
workouts.riskReason: A 30-minute continuous run with threshold segments introduces solid muscle fatigue.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Pickups at target threshold effort; recovery sections at relaxed conversational pace.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high Zone 2, rising to Zone 3 inside pickups.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization Warm-up
warmup.description: 5 mins of easy walking and mobilization.

mainSet.name: 30-Min Continuous Fartlek
mainSet.description: Run 30 minutes continuously, incorporating 8 × 1-min pickups at threshold effort with a 2-min easy jog recovery between each pickup.

easier.description: Reduce running duration to 20 minutes continuous, with 5 pickups.

mainSet.name: 20-Min Fartlek
mainSet.description: Run 20 minutes continuously with 5 × 1-min pickups.

harder.description: Increase running duration to 40 minutes continuous, with 12 pickups.

mainSet.name: 40-Min Fartlek
mainSet.description: Run 40 minutes continuously with 12 × 1-min pickups.

coachingNotes: The pickups should feel controlled. Think of them as 'comfortably hard' rather than sprints.
Prioritize a smooth, conversational rhythm for your base jog segments.
Great for building physical and mental pacing discipline.
commonMistakes: Running the base jog segments too fast, leading to redlining.
safetyNotes: Maintain tall, erect posture even as fatigue sets in.
Ensure you are fully hydrated before starting.

shareCard.purposeText: A continuous run incorporating threshold pickups to build aerobic limits safely.

workouts.sourceNote: General running training principles; not personalized medical or coaching advice.

workouts.title: Intermediate Out-and-Back Progressive Fartlek
workouts.summary: A 40-minute out-and-back run where the return leg incorporates structured pickups to practice running faster when tired.
workouts.riskReason: Structured progressive workouts on pre-fatigued legs carry a moderate orthopedic risk.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Outward leg conversational jog; return leg incorporates pickups at target 10K/threshold pace.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Low Zone 2 outward; progressive spikes to High Zone 3 return.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization Warm-up
warmup.description: 5 mins light joint mobility dynamics and stretching.

mainSet.name: Outward Leg: Easy Jog
mainSet.description: Run 20 minutes outward continuously at a relaxed conversational pace.

mainSet.name: Return Leg: 5 × 2-Min Pickups
mainSet.description: Run 20 minutes return continuously, incorporating 5 × 2-min pickups at 10K effort, separated by 2-min easy jog recoveries.

easier.description: Reduce to 30 minutes total: 15m out, 15m back with 3 × 2-min pickups.

mainSet.name: Outward Leg: Easy Jog
mainSet.description: Run 15 minutes easy.

mainSet.name: Return Leg: 3 × 2-Min Pickups
mainSet.description: Run 15 minutes with 3 pickups.

harder.description: Increase to 50 minutes total: 25m out, 25m back with 6 × 2-min pickups.

mainSet.name: Outward Leg: Easy Jog
mainSet.description: Run 25 minutes easy.

mainSet.name: Return Leg: 6 × 2-Min Pickups
mainSet.description: Run 25 minutes with 6 pickups.

coachingNotes: Pacing discipline is key. Do not race the outward leg.
Use the first pickup on the return leg to establish a smooth rhythm.
Practice focusing on a steady breath rhythm as muscles tire.
commonMistakes: Running the outward leg too aggressively, leaving minimal energy for return pickups.
Shortening recoveries on the return leg.
safetyNotes: Stop immediately if sharp musculoskeletal pain occurs.
Stay alert to footing during fast segments.

shareCard.purposeText: A 40-minute out-and-back session to practice progressive pacing when tired.

workouts.title: Advanced Long Aerobic Float Fartlek

workouts.riskReason: Sustained high-effort tempo blocks with active float recoveries carry moderate fatigue risks.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Pickups at target half marathon tempo effort; recoveries are active float jogs, not walking.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Spike to high Zone 3 during pickups; maintain high Zone 2 during float segments.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization Warm-up
warmup.description: 5 mins of easy walking and mobility dynamics.

mainSet.name: 50-Min Float Fartlek
mainSet.description: Run 50 minutes continuously, incorporating 6 × 3-min pickups at target half marathon effort, separated by 3-min steady active float recovery jogs.

easier.description: Reduce running duration to 40 minutes continuous, with 5 pickups.

mainSet.name: 40-Min Float Fartlek
mainSet.description: Run 40 minutes continuously with 5 × 3-min pickups.

harder.description: Increase running duration to 60 minutes continuous, with 8 pickups.

mainSet.name: 60-Min Float Fartlek
mainSet.description: Run 60 minutes continuously with 8 × 3-min pickups.

coachingNotes: Focus on active float recovery jogs. Do not walk or stop.
Great for building physical and mental durability.
Keep the upper body fully relaxed during tempo segments.
commonMistakes: Running the pickups too fast, forcing walking recoveries.
safetyNotes: Carry hydration or plan routes with water access.
Stop immediately if you feel joint or tendon pain.

shareCard.purposeText: A sustained 50-minute session utilizing float recoveries to build stamina.

mainSet.name: Single Mona Block

mainSet.name: Elite Double Mona

safetyNotes: Carry hydration or plan routes with water access.
